basisOfRecord.quote: To examine the patterns of ant diversity along elevational gradients, we conducted field surveys in the Qinling Mountains, a natural boundary between the warm temperate and subtropical zones in China.
We conducted this study in July 2021.

To collect epigaeic ants, we set up three pitfall traps (diameter: 65 mm; depth: 77 mm; volume: 160 ml) filled with conserving liquid (ethanol and ethylene glycol, 1:1, approximately 50 ml) and one paper trap (baited with tuna and honey) using a 297 mm × 420 mm white paper.

Following the methods outlined in the literature (Liu et al. 2016; Nooten et al. 2021), we constructed our ant community phylogenetic tree based on the phylogenetic tree with 269 ant genera worldwide from Economo et al. (2018).

measurementStatistic.quote: The functional traits of ant communities at low and high elevation were similar (larger body sizes, wider heads, longer scapes, bigger eyes, longer mandibles and longer hind legs), while ants at the middle elevation showed opposite traits.
In total, we measured 187 individuals representing 42 ant species, and we provided the details of these measurements in Table S4.
